name: Tom Steyer
role: Billionaire investor and climate activist; 2020 Democratic presidential candidate; 2026 California governor candidate
summary: Tom Steyer is a billionaire investor who made climate change his main cause and ran for the 2020 Democratic presidential nomination on a platform of climate action, a wealth tax, term limits and a national referendum process. He ran for California governor in 2026, campaigning on taxing the wealthy, abolishing ICE and free public education, and he has moved to support single-payer health care.

sources.title: What does Tom Steyer believe? Where the candidate stands on the issues
sources.author: PBS NewsHour
sources.usedFor: Quotes his 2017 Netroots Nation vow that NextGen would not work for a candidate who is not pro-choice

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: His criminal justice plan reforms policing (community policing, a federal use-of-force standard, demilitarization) rather than abolishing it.

abortion-legal.rationale: In 2017 at Netroots Nation he said 'We're pro-choice' and that his group would not work for any candidate who is not pro-choice, as reported by Politico. The remarks are about his political group's stance rather than a direct personal statement on abortion law.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: He called Israel's annexation of the Jordan Valley and 30 percent of the West Bank a violation of international law that he opposes.

ban-cartels.rationale: Pledged to 'break up utility monopolies' to lower electricity rates (2026). This is limited to utilities rather than cartels in general.

corporate-influence.rationale: Said the plan would 'break the stranglehold that corporations exercise over our government with their money and lobbying power' (October 2019), and that corporations are not people.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: In the debates he said he is for reparations to African Americans and would set up a formal commission on race on day one to "repair damage that's been done officially".

death-penalty.rationale: Publicly supported Proposition 62 in 2016, the ballot measure to end capital punishment in California, via a press release.

direct-votes.rationale: His July 2019 plan called for an annual national referendum process on major issues, letting voters decide directly rather than through Congress.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Campaign platform: 'Declaring the climate crisis a national emergency on day one' and net-zero warming pollution by 2045; he called climate 'priority one'.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: In a debate he said the United States has committed to treating everybody equally, in education and at work, including people with disabilities.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Asked about nuclear power in a debate, he said it is not price-competitive, carries disaster risks, and leaves waste that cannot be stored; he did not call for building new plants.

free-public-college.rationale: Campaign issue headline in 2026: 'Provide Free Education From Pre-K to College'. The 2020 platform also called for pre-K through college education as a basic right.

human-caused-global-warming.rationale: He described the climate crisis as the unintended consequence of an economy built on fossil fuels and made cutting fossil-fuel pollution to net zero the core of his plan.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: His working-families tax plan expands the Earned Income Tax Credit by about 25% and makes the Child Tax Credit fully refundable with an extra credit for children under six.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: He said any peace plan must guarantee Israel's peace and security alongside a real roadmap to a two-state solution.

limit-guns.rationale: His gun plan calls for a national license for all gun ownership, a registry of existing and a ban on new assault weapons, universal background checks, waiting periods and safe-storage rules.

no-business-privileges.rationale: His plan ends government giveaways to big polluters and says corporations that "write their own rules" must be held in check.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Told the AP in 2026 that anyone unwilling to pay 'your fair share' is 'spitting on those people'. This is a general statement about the duty of the wealthy to contribute to the public, not about looking after the less fortunate.

public-ownership.rationale: His economic agenda says inequality should be addressed "not by nationalizing industries but rather by fixing what is broken with our capitalist system", and that socialism is not the answer.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: In February 2020 he vowed to call for a $22 federal hourly minimum wage, reported in a news account of his campaign event.

recognize-territorial-claims-from-conque.rationale: He opposed unilateral annexation of West Bank territory as contrary to international law.

reduce-immigration.rationale: His immigration plan creates a pathway to citizenship for undocumented residents, reinvigorates the asylum and refugee system and recruits foreign talent, while saying borders should be protected.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Campaign plans call for breaking 'the stranglehold that corporations exercise over our government' and for reforms on corporate money and lobbying; this points toward tighter regulation of corporate influence, though not a general regulatory agenda he stated.

rehabilitation.rationale: His criminal justice plan prioritizes rehabilitation behind bars and in re-entry, with education, Pell Grants for prisoners and treatment instead of incarceration for drug offenders.

slavery-reparations.rationale: He said in the February 2020 New Hampshire debate: "I am for reparations to African Americans in this country."

social-market-economy.rationale: He calls himself "a progressive and a capitalist": a market economy kept fair by government guardrails, with a public option, tax credits and a minimum wage.

student-debt-relief.rationale: His economic agenda forgives student loan debt of teachers and other public servants and refinances other loans at lower rates, which is partial relief.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Called Trump's trade war 'a failure, hurting working Americans, hurting businesses, killing farmers' (October 2019). This opposes tariffs as used in that trade war, not tariffs in general.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Proposed a 1% annual tax on net worth above $32 million (October 2019) and, in 2026, said 'I'm the billionaire who wants to tax other billionaires' while supporting a one-time billionaire tax.

term-limits.rationale: Proposed 12-year term limits for members of Congress and the Senate, plus congressional term limits in his 2019 political reform plan.

turn-back-illegal-migrants.rationale: His plan ends family separation and detention abuses and extends compassion to those fleeing persecution through reformed asylum, which is at odds with turning border-crossers back at once.

unions-good.rationale: His economic agenda pledges to foster the growth and organizational strength of public- and private-sector unions and to protect the right to organize.

universal-healthcare.rationale: In December 2025 he said 'Bernie Sanders was right. We need single-payer health care.' In 2019-2020 he opposed Medicare for All and backed an opt-in public option instead; the later statement is used as his most recent clear position.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: He said unchecked capitalism and corporate money have hijacked democracy and called income inequality unbearable and unjust, backing a wealth tax.

notes: Health care changed over time: he opposed Medicare for All and backed a public option in 2019-2020, then in December 2025 said 'We need single-payer health care' and used the most recent statement. Most of the known answers come from his 2019-2020 campaign releases (American Presidency Project copies) and his 2026 issue page and reported remarks. Many statements are left null: the reviewed sources did not address them. Searches on unions, drug policy, Israel/Iran beyond the 2020 statement, and abortion beyond 2017 found too little usable text. Attempts to fetch the 2026 Substack ICE post and the Davis Vanguard interview failed (403) and the Bloomberg Law article was paywalled, so those are reported only through secondary coverage and Wikipedia. Two campaign-era items (the 2020 criminal justice plan and the 2019 marijuana interview) were found only in pages that could not be fetched, so they are not used. Pass 2 (claude-sonnet-5-5, 2026-11-19): searched his 2019-20 presidential campaign plans (economy, health care, climate, criminal justice, guns, immigration, taxes), five Democratic debates (Nov 2019-Feb 2020), Israel/Palestine statements and 2026 governor coverage; answered 34 statements. He has no recorded position on religion and state, nationalism, secession and minority autonomy, constitutional design or war powers beyond the debate remarks cited, so those stay null and the uncertainty rule is not met.
